subject: science
intro: Carbon atoms cycle among Earth's systems. Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and stores the carbon in sugars in living things (the biosphere). Cellular respiration releases carbon back to the atmosphere as carbon dioxide. Carbon also moves into the hydrosphere (dissolved in oceans) and the geosphere (as fossil fuels and rock). Burning fossil fuels releases stored carbon back to the atmosphere. Photosynthesis and respiration are two key processes that move carbon between living things and the air.

items.prompt: How do photosynthesis and cellular respiration move carbon in opposite directions?

steps: Photosynthesis takes carbon dioxide out of the air and stores the carbon in sugars.
Cellular respiration breaks down sugars and releases carbon dioxide back to the air.
So photosynthesis removes carbon from the air and respiration returns it, moving carbon in opposite directions.
solution.answer: Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the air into sugars, while respiration releases carbon dioxide back, moving carbon oppositely.

items.prompt: Trace one carbon atom from the air into a plant and then into an animal.

steps: Photosynthesis takes a carbon dioxide molecule from the air and builds the carbon into sugar in the plant.
An animal eats the plant and takes in that carbon as part of the sugar.
So the carbon moves from the air (atmosphere) into the plant and then into the animal (biosphere).
solution.answer: Carbon moves from air to plant through photosynthesis, then into the animal when it eats the plant.

items.prompt: How does burning fossil fuels affect the carbon cycle?

steps: Fossil fuels store carbon that came from ancient living things, held in the geosphere.
Burning them releases that carbon as carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.
So burning fossil fuels adds extra carbon dioxide to the air, affecting the carbon cycle.
solution.answer: Burning fossil fuels releases stored carbon from the geosphere as carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.

items.prompt: Which process removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere?

steps: Removing carbon dioxide from the air happens in plants.

items.prompt: Name the four Earth systems that carbon cycles among.

steps: Carbon moves among the major Earth systems.
They are the biosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere, and geosphere.
solution.answer: The biosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere, and geosphere.

items.prompt: Develop a model showing carbon cycling between the atmosphere and biosphere using photosynthesis and respiration.

steps: Show carbon dioxide in the atmosphere being taken in by plants through photosynthesis.
Show the carbon stored in living things (biosphere) and released by respiration.
The arrows loop: photosynthesis moves carbon from air to life, respiration moves it back, forming a cycle.
solution.answer: Photosynthesis moves carbon from the atmosphere into the biosphere, and respiration moves it back, forming a cycle.
